text:
Connor O'Brien: heads up: scheduling staged rollout for hot-route capacity protection (tier-aware throttling + enterprise lanes). Want to confirm region order + rollback triggers + who’s holding the levers.

Connor O'Brien: Proposed rollout (all times PT):
- Tue 10:00–11:30: canary only (prod-canary routers + 1 gateway shard) in us-east-1
- Tue 12:00–13:00: us-east-1 10% -> 50% -> 100% (15 min soak each)
- Wed 10:00–12:00: us-west-2 same ramp
- Thu 10:00–12:00: eu-central-1 same ramp
- Fri: ap-southeast-1 if signals are clean (optional)

Connor O'Brien: Feature flags:
- `hot_route_protection_enabled` (global)
- `enterprise_lane_enabled` (router)
- `gateway_per_route_rl_enabled` (gateway)
Kill switch is `hot_route_protection_enabled=false` (should disable both routing + gateway enforcement paths, leaving only metrics).

Benji Okafor: yep flags are wired that way post pr-18471. kill switch is immediate at gateway (poll 5s) and router (poll 10s). config propagation worst case 60s.

Rafael Mendes: +1. For rollback triggers, can we be explicit so oncall doesn’t debate mid-event?

Connor O'Brien: yes pls. here’s what I have drafted:
1) Enterprise lane p99 latency regression > 20% for 10 min vs baseline (per-route, top enterprise routes only)
2) 5xx rate increase > 0.3% absolute for 5 min (gateway or router)
3) “unexpected” 429 spike: enterprise tier throttled_count > 0.1% of requests for 5 min (we should basically never throttle enterprise except extreme fleet loss)
4) Router queue depth sustained > threshold (Mina’s team suggested 2x normal) + tail latency rising

Mina Haddad: for (4) I’d rather key on admission reject reasons vs raw queue depth. queue depth is noisy w/ long prompts. can we use `admit_deny_reason=backpressure_hard` > 0.5% for 5 min? that’s basically “we’re shedding because runtime says we’re saturated”.

Aisha Bello: dashboards are ready w/ those labels. here’s the lane view: https://grafana.prod.redwood/d/lanes-hot-route (enterprise vs standard) and per-route SLO: https://grafana.prod.redwood/d/slo-per-route-tier

Sergio Costa: alert routing note: I can temporarily silence the “throttling spike” page during the planned ramp if we agree it’s expected for self-serve. but we should NOT silence enterprise lane alerts.

Sean Gallagher: agree. for canary window, we should page only on (2) and enterprise (1)/(3). self-serve throttling will go up by design.

Amara Diallo: gateway side: 429 semantics + `Retry-After` are in. biggest risk is clients retrying aggressively and causing thundering herd. we should watch `retry_after_ignored_estimate` (approx via same request-id pattern) but it’s best-effort.

Jordan Lee: policy engine has safe defaults. note: if policy config fetch fails, gateway is fail-open for rate limits (per ADR) but router lane separation still works. so rollback might be less effective in that failure mode. we should monitor config fetch error too.

Connor O'Brien: good call. adding rollback trigger:
5) policy config fetch error rate > 1% for 5 min in any region during ramp (because it invalidates enforcement assumptions)

Benji Okafor: +1. also remember we have “enforcement mode” knob in config:
- `observe_only` (metrics only)
- `enforce`
we’re going canary `observe_only` for 15 min then flip `enforce`.

Talia Benson: ownership: who is DRI per region? (i need to update the program brief + comms)

Rafael Mendes: I can DRI the us-east-1 and us-west-2 ramps (SRE). Connor for the actual release steps + coordination. Mina/Amara on standby for router/gateway issues.

Connor O'Brien: works. I’ll run the checklist + flip flags. Rafael is “go/no-go” based on graphs.

Mina Haddad: router oncall that week is Elena, but I’ll be around for the first ramp. can we schedule the actual flip at :05 past so we don’t collide w/ the hourly batch jobs? minor but helps.

Connor O'Brien: yep. ramp steps at 10:05 / 10:25 / 10:45 etc.

Sergio Costa: alert tuning: for the ramp, I’ll pin these panels in the incident view:
- `router_admit_deny_total{lane=enterprise}`
- `gateway_http_responses_total{code="429",tier="enterprise"}`
- `request_p99_ms{tier="enterprise"}`
- `policy_fetch_failures_total`

Aisha Bello: also adding a note on the dashboard w/ expected behavior: self-serve 429 up is ok; enterprise 429 should stay ~0. and enterprise should see *lower* tail lat if we’re shedding lower tiers.

DeployBot: Deploy scheduled: prod-router canary (us-east-1) build redwood-router@18436 + policy@18444 + backpressure@18457. Window: 2025-01-26 10:00–11:30 PT.

Connor O'Brien: thanks. canary deploy first, then we’ll flip `enterprise_lane_enabled` only, soak, then flip `gateway_per_route_rl_enabled`, soak, then `hot_route_protection_enabled` (global). we want to isolate.

Rafael Mendes: can we simplify? `hot_route_protection_enabled` being the kill switch is good, but the staged enable makes debugging much easier. keep as is.

Amara Diallo: +1. gateway enable first w/out router lanes will change 429 patterns; router lanes first w/out gateway limits changes admission. staged is the way.

Connor O'Brien: rollback plan (confirming):
- immediate: set `hot_route_protection_enabled=false` (kill)
- if only gateway misbehaves: set `gateway_per_route_rl_enabled=false`
- if only router lanes misbehave: set `enterprise_lane_enabled=false`
- if config is bad: revert policy to last-known-good (Benji can do) + keep in observe_only

Benji Okafor: yep. LKG snapshot is stored w/ checksum. revert is one command: `policyctl promote --env prod --version <hash>`.

Sean Gallagher: please link runbook section for oncall so we don’t rely on tribal knowledge.

Connor O'Brien: runbook: https://confluence.redwood/pages/overload-throttling-and-priority-routing-response (section “Rollout / rollback steps” is updated). I’ll also paste the exact flag commands in the change ticket.

Talia Benson: for proactive comms: CS asked whether regions will be rolled one at a time. answer: yes, region-by-region w/ 24h soak, and we’ll notify top accounts once us-east is stable.

Rafael Mendes: last question: what’s the success criteria to proceed from us-east to us-west? we should be clear.

Connor O'Brien: propose:
- enterprise p95/p99 within 10% of baseline (or better)
- enterprise 429 < 0.05% sustained
- no increase in 5xx
- self-serve throttling increase is acceptable if overall fleet health improves (GPU util / queue depth stable)

Mina Haddad: add: no sustained `backpressure_hard` rejects above 0.5% in enterprise lane.

Sergio Costa: ok, I’ll add a temporary annotation on all the dashboards at each flip so postmortem is easy.

Aisha Bello: I’ll stay on for us-east ramp and validate SLO burn-rate alerts don’t flap.

Connor O'Brien: cool. locking schedule unless someone objects. i’ll post a reminder 30m before canary + open a war-room thread in #incidents only if we trip rollback triggers.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: good.

Benji Okafor: :thumbsup: (and pls don’t forget to flip back alert silences after canary)

Sergio Costa: lol yes, I’ll set them w/ explicit expiry.

Connor O'Brien: done. thanks all.
